biography.plain_text: Sheikh Hamdan bin Zayed Al Nahyan is an Emirati royal and public official serving as the Ruler's Representative in Abu Dhabi's Al Dhafra Region. A son of UAE founder Sheikh Zayed, he previously held federal foreign-affairs and deputy-prime-minister posts and now chairs major environmental, humanitarian and higher-education institutions across Abu Dhabi and the UAE.

long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Al Ain in 1963, Sheikh Hamdan bin Zayed Al Nahyan is a son of Sheikh Zayed, the UAE's founding president. After degrees in political science and business administration from United Arab Emirates University, he entered federal service, becoming foreign-ministry undersecretary, minister of state for foreign affairs and then deputy prime minister. He was appointed the Abu Dhabi Ruler's Representative in the Western Region in 2009, now known as Al Dhafra.

His present public work spans regional administration, conservation, humanitarian relief and education. He chairs the Environment Agency - Abu Dhabi, Emirates Red Crescent and Abu Dhabi University's board of trustees, roles that connect environmental policy, aid and higher education. Public reporting also identifies him as owner of Yas, a 141-metre motor yacht created in Abu Dhabi through the extensive conversion of a former Dutch naval frigate.
